segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Hey Dana, yeah, thanks for making time. I wanted to walk through the final quote and make sure we're clean for signature by Friday.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Sure. I have about 20 minutes. The main things are seats, invoice timing, and making sure legal has the right order form.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep. So current quote is 32 seats, annual term, $38,400 total. We kept the services line at $4,800 for onboarding and admin training.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay, that's the number I have. Billing starts May 1, right? Our finance team doesn't want an April invoice.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Correct, May 1 subscription start, net 30 terms. The billing tool will generate the first invoice after the countersignature, but dated May 1.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Got it. One thing, the onboarding worksheet that came over this morning still says 25 seats and April 18 go-live. We moved that to 32 seats and April 25 when we talked Friday.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Ah, yeah, sorry about that. The quote is right, but that worksheet is off. I'll get it corrected today before the kickoff invite goes out.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Thanks. I just don't want our ops lead planning around the wrong date. April 25 is the earliest we can have the data file ready.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Understood. I'll note April 25 as the target go-live and April 15 for the file handoff. Anything else in the contract language holding you up?

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: No, legal was okay with the standard renewal clause as long as the price increase cap stays at 5 percent. Send the updated order form and we should be able to sign tomorrow.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Perfect. I'll send it over by 3 today with the 32 seats, May 1 billing start, and the 5 percent cap called out.
